commit_reviews.summary: Solid cross-cutting commit — Flask-Limiter with a user-aware key function, Redis-backed storage defaulting to MemoryStorage for tests, and keyset cursor pagination pushed into the repository layer, all covered by updated and new tests.

compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the tier-2 multi-file seed entirely and rebuilt as a flat single file, throwing away the seed's Blueprint structure, users/items schema, and existing auth utilities — a deliberate reset that Session 4's repository refactor had to reconstruct from scratch
Session 2 hand-rolled JWT (HMAC-SHA256 via hmac/base64) instead of using a library like PyJWT; this hand-rolled token path persisted through all later sessions and every auth route depends on it

Session 2's migration used the username column as the user's contact/email address for notifications (tests register 'alice@example.com' as a username), a schema compromise that leaked into Session 3's notification design
Binary artifacts leaked into git history: tasks.db, __pycache__/*.pyc, and tests/__pycache__ were committed in Sessions 2, 4, and 5 instead of being gitignored
Repository layer builds SQL via f-string interpolation (table/column names from class attributes); values are parameterized so not exploitable, but the pattern is fragile to future refactors
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield rewrite — a minimal SQLite-only task API (create/list/get/update) with no auth, replacing the seed wholesale
Session 2 introduced per-user task ownership (owner_id + idempotent migration that backfills a 'legacy' user) and JWT auth — this became the core domain invariant all later sessions preserved
Session 2's choose-your-own hand-rolled JWT implementation, since auth was built without any external JWT dependency
Session 4's repository pattern (abstract BaseRepository + TaskRepository/UserRepository) extracted from routes, which gave Session 5 a clean seam to layer pagination and rate limiting onto
Session 5 added production cross-cutting concerns: Redis-backed Flask-Limiter with a MemoryStorage test fallback (so tests never require Redis) and cursor-based pagination for GET /tasks
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically across all five sessions. Session 1 delivered a flat, unauthenticated task CRUD API; Session 2 raised the floor with JWT auth, password hashing, and per-user task ownership including a backfill migration; Session 3 added asynchronous Celery completion notifications triggered only on genuine pending->completed transitions; Session 4 restructured the persistence layer into a clean repository hierarchy, shrinking app.py by ~110 lines; Session 5 capped it with rate limiting and cursor pagination with robust validation. Test coverage grew from zero tests at Session 1 to 10 test functions / 13 assertions-cases by Session 5, and pytest was green after every commit. The only regression in arc was Session 1 discarding the seed's structure, which Session 4 later repaired through the repository refactor.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-sequenced build where auth and ownership (S2) enabled notifications (S3), the repository refactor (S4) enabled cross-cutting rate limiting and pagination (S5), with steadily expanding green tests throughout.
